newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Oil refinery plans for PNG progress slowly.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Oil refinery plans for PNG progress slowly.

text.p: Little progress has been made on the proposed development of three oil refineries in Papua New Guinea, commercial sources in Port Moresby told Reuters.
The main refinery, proposed for Motukea Island near Port Moresby, was still waiting for finance, an official with Curtain Brothers Papua New Guinea Pty Ltd told Reuters.
Australia-based Curtain Brothers is a main proposer of the project. "At this stage the finance is still being organised for a feasibility study," the official said.

A second refinery, called Kopi and proposed for the Gulf of Papua where a pipeline from the Kutubu oilfield reaches the southern islands, had not met government pre-qualification requirements, the Curtain Brothers official said.
This refinery is proposed by the U.S. Galveston-Houston Co of Texas, which said last year the project was designed to process 30,000 barrels of crude oil a day.
Galveston-Houston said it would hold 25 percent of the operating company, PNG Oil Refinery Co Pty Ltd.
A third refinery now being suggested, called Napa Napa and proposed for Port Moresby harbour, is based on use of a second-hand equipment.
A variety of industry sources contacted in Port Moresby said that discord surrounded all of the proposed refineries.
A main problem was long delays with the Motukea refinery and differences of views between government departments, they said.
